report.source_text: Although steroid therapy was initiated, further cardiac investigations were necessary to identify the cause of arrythmias on the fourth day after steroid pulse therapy initiation. Since cardiac magnetic resonance imaging was not suitable under transvenous temporary pacing, we performed cardiac catheterization. Coronary angiography confirmed no coronary artery stenosis; therefore, we performed an endomyocardial biopsy of the right ventricular septum. This revealed that CD3-positive lymphocytes and CD163-positive macrophages had infiltrated the interstitium adjacent to the degenerated and necrotic myocytes, which showed localized immunopositivity for programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) (Fig. 3). In addition, immunostaining for tenascin-C, a known marker for inflammation, was positive in the interstitium adjacent to the necrotic myocytes (Fig. 3).

The trajectory is strongly supported by: (1) temporal relationship with pembrolizumab exposure, (2) elevated cardiac biomarkers (troponin I 0.032 ng/mL, NT-proBNP 1,724 pg/mL), (3) preserved ejection fraction on echocardiography without structural abnormalities (consistent with conduction-system-focused myocarditis), (4) dramatic response to pulse steroid therapy with improvement in eGFR, normalization of biomarkers, and resolution of arrhythmias, and (5) histopathologic evidence of CD3+ lymphocytes and CD163+ macrophages infiltrating myocardium with PD-L1 immunopositivity and tenascin-C positivity indicating ICI-induced inflammation. Additional temporal and clinical course details would complete the trajectory reconstruction.

clinician.final_diagnosis: ICI-induced myocarditis with sinus node damage causing sick sinus syndrome
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old woman with cT4N2M1 squamous cell lung carcinoma on pembrolizumab monotherapy developed high fever (CTCAE grade 1) and acute kidney injury (eGFR decline from 72 to 39 mL/min/1.73 m²; CTCAE grade 3) after the second pembrolizumab dose. ECG monitoring revealed frequent sinus pauses (~5 seconds) and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, consistent with sick sinus syndrome (CTCAE grade 3). Cardiac biomarkers were elevated: troponin I 0.032 ng/mL (normal ≤0.026) and NT-proBNP 1,724 pg/mL (normal ≤125). Echocardiography showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (60-65%) without wall motion abnormalities, pericardial effusion, or valvular disease. Pulse steroid therapy was initiated, resulting in rapid clinical improvement: increased eGFR, decreased troponin I and NT-proBNP levels, reduction in sinus pause frequency, and complete resolution of atrial fibrillation. Endomyocardial biopsy of the right ventricular septum performed on day 4 after steroid initiation revealed CD3-positive lymphocytes and CD163-positive macrophages infiltrating the interstitium adjacent to degenerated and necrotic myocytes with localized PD-L1 immunopositivity and tenascin-C positivity, confirming ICI-induced myocarditis. Coronary angiography excluded coronary artery stenosis as an alternative etiology.
